issues.failure_explanation: The normalizer is a pointwise affine map (x-mu_x)/sigma_x, i.e. a diagonal rescaling in physical space. It turns covariance C into D^{-1}CD^{-1}, which keeps the correlation and spectral decay. It neither whitens nor erases correlation structure; the remark asserts both. For the Fourier-diagonal periodic prior the pointwise variance is constant, so the normalizer is a scalar rescaling that cannot change relative high-frequency content. The paper uses this whitening/preconditioning to explain why the white reference performs well in Encode-only, and that explanation is unsupported.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's averaged velocity comes from the independent linear interpolation, with z_0=x (target) and z_1=xi (reference). The invoked theorem bounds the Föllmer velocity, which belongs to a different interpolation with the opposite orientation (reference to target). The bound cannot hold for the paper's field. At tau=0, v(z,0)=E[xi-x|z_0=z]=-z because xi is centred and independent, so Lip=1, whereas the theorem requires Lip<=L_0*0=0. Conversely, if w averages the Föllmer field with the Mean-Flow convention z_r=z_t-(t-r)w, then T(xi)=xi-w(xi;0,1) maps the time-1 (target) state to time 0, i.e., the wrong direction. issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated on a separable infinite-dimensional H with a trace-class (compact, non-invertible) reference covariance, but the cited result is finite-dimensional. In infinite dimensions, N(0,C) has no Lebesgue density, and the assumption involves the unbounded C^{-1} and B^{-1}. diagnostic_evidence.quote: :=&\frac{1}{t-r}\int_r^t v(z_\tau,\tau)\mathrm{d}\tau

issues.failure_explanation: As a function of the state z at time t, w averages v(Phi_{t->tau}(z),tau), where Phi is the flow map. Its Lipschitz constant therefore involves Lip(v)*Lip(Phi), and Lip(Phi) can exceed 1. Counterexample satisfying Lip(v(tau,.))<=L_0 tau: take v(tau,x)=-L_0 tau x. Then z_0=e^{L_0/2}xi, so w(xi;0,1)=(1-e^{L_0/2})xi with Lip=e^{L_0/2}-1>L_0/2, and Lip(T)=e^{L_0/2}>1+L_0/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use Grönwall: T is the flow map Phi_{1->0}, so Lip(T)<=exp(L_0/2). Then Lip(w(.;0,1))<=1+exp(L_0/2), with analogous bounds for general (r,t). Restate the lemma, corollary and main theorem with these dimension-free constants.
issues.overall_effect: The stated constants L_0(t+r)/2, L_0/2 and 1+L_0/2 are false in general.
issues.title: Lipschitz bound for averaged velocity ignores flow-map composition
issues.why_classification: A standard argument restores dimension-free Lipschitz continuity, but the stated quantitative bounds must be replaced by exponentially larger ones.
